item.title: Venus Williams Loses 16th Straight: A Look Into the Decline
item.description: Aug 14, 2023; Mason, OH, USA; Venus Williams concentrates on her shot as she faces Veronika Kudermetova during round one of the Western & Southern Open at the Lindner Family Tennis Center in Mason Monday, August, 14, 2023. Mandatory Credit: Cara Owsley… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Jim Smith Venus Williams has now lost 16 consecutive matches, the latest to an 18-year-old who was born the same year Williams won her last Grand Slam title. The former World #1 ranks sixth in career singles wins with 819, including 49 titles and seven Grand Slam championships. But she hasn’t won a title since February 2016, and the results since have been difficult to watch. A Historic Age Gap Lilli Tagger , 18, defeated Williams 6-2 6-2 at the Guangzhou Open earlier this week, dropping the 46-year-old to 0-13 in 2026. The match set a WTA record for the largest age gap between opponents at 28 years. Tagger was born in 2008, the same year Williams won her last major singles title at Wimbledon. The Austrian hit 29 winners to Williams’ seven, never faced a break point and won 25 of 25 first-serve points. Williams was broken four times with relative ease. It was not an outlier. Williams has won just four of 30 sets this season and has often looked uncompetitive. Her 2026 campaign includes two losses to players outside the top-350, and m0re than half of her defeats have come against players ranked outside the top-75. She holds an 8-46 record on Tour since 2020 and has just one win since 2023. “I’ve Earned the Right” Williams addressed the streak after the loss to Tagger. “Well, obviously 0-16 isn’t ideal,” she said . “I’m a competitor. I’ve been a competitor my entire life, and nobody likes losing, certainly not me … Maybe other people don’t understand it, but I do … I think I’ve earned the right to decide how this ends.” She also spoke about the health challenges she has faced. Williams was diagnosed with Sjögren’s syndrome and has dealt with fibroids, which forced a long break in 2011, when she was ranked top five in doubles. Being able to play and practice pain-free, she said, is a motivator she doesn’t take for granted. She has no plans to retire anytime soon. “Will I still be playing in six months? A year? Two years? Who knows?” she said . “I certainly don’t have a date circled on the calendar. But right now, I’m happy. I’m enjoying being on the court, I’m enjoying the work with my team, and physically I’m in a place where I can do that. So while I feel this way, I’ll continue.” A Decline Years in the Making The numbers tell a story of steady erosion since her last title at the 2016 Taiwan Open . Williams reached three finals in 2017, including the Australian Open against her sister Serena. In 2018, she reached only one semifinal, and in 2019 she managed just four quarterfinals. Though, it serves as a testament to the depth of her career that her tour winning percentage has only slipped from .765 to .737 since 2020. A Career Worth Celebrating Jan 19, 2011; Melbour

Viktor Arvidsson Gets Ultimate Compliment From Todd McLellan
item.description: The Detroit Red Wings may have found one of the best bargains of the NHL offseason, and head coach Todd McLellan is making it clear just how much Viktor Arvidsson means to his team. Arvidsson delivered a sensational performance Thursday night, recording three goals and an assist in Detroit’s 4-1 victory over the Chicago Blackhawks at Little Caesars Arena. It was the veteran forward’s sixth career hat trick and his first wearing the Winged Wheel. And afterward, McLellan had some pretty strong praise for the 33-year-old. Oct 17, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Red Wings left wing Viktor Arvidsson (33) looks on during the second period against the San Jose Sharks at Little Caesars Arena. Mandatory Credit: Brian Bradshaw Sevald-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Todd McLellan Praises Viktor Arvidsson Following Hat Trick While Arvidsson’s three goals stole the headlines, McLellan was quick to point out that his impact extends well beyond the scoresheet. “(Arvidsson)’s a hell of a hockey player, but what he brings to the table night in and night out is that competitiveness,” McLellan said following Thursday’s victory . “And you can see it. His engine doesn’t stop. When he’s not scoring, he’s hunting and he’s turning pucks over.” That’s exactly the kind of player Detroit hoped it was getting when it signed Arvidsson to a two-year, $10 million contract during the offseason. As we previously reported , Arvidsson was already proving to be a bargain before Thursday’s breakout performance. Now, through 13 games, he has eight goals and six assists for 14 points. Not bad for a player earning $5 million per season. Viktor Arvidsson Loving His Role With Red Wings Arvidsson was equally enthusiastic when asked about how things have gone since arriving in Detroit. “I’m not going to lie, it’s fun. I’m just trying to do my part, work hard and try to go to the net as much as I can. Playing with (DeBrincat) and (Emmitt Finnie) has been working really well. I’m just trying to play my game.” That chemistry was on full display against Chicago. Alex DeBrincat assisted on Arvidsson’s first two goals, while Finnie set up his empty-netter to complete the hat trick. Arvidsson also credited the entire team for responding after Chicago took an early lead. “I think we played a really good game, the whole team. And just like in Edmonton, we found a way to get going there. I think our second and third period there were outstanding.” Detroit has now earned at least one point in eight of its last nine games, improving to 6-4-3. Red Wings May Have Found Perfect Fit Perhaps the most encouraging part of Arvidsson’s performance is how naturally he’s fitting alongside DeBrincat and Finnie. With Dylan Larkin no longer in the lineup, Detroit desperately needs forwards capable of generating consistent offense. Arvidsson is doing exactly that. item.title: The Chicago Bears Got Jeffery Simmons but Now Comes the Hard Part
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Chicago Bears got the player they wanted. The harder question is what they gave up to get him. Chicago acquired All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from Tennessee on Thursday, sending the Titans first-round picks in 2027 and 2028 and a 2027 fourth-round pick. The Bears also received a 2028 fifth-round pick. It is a huge price for a 29-year-old defender, even one capable of changing how opponents block Chicago’s front. Simmons makes the Bears better today. He had 11 sacks last season and has four through seven games this year. ESPN’s analysis identified the need clearly: Chicago ranked 23rd in pass-rush win rate from its interior defenders before the trade, while Simmons led NFL defensive tackles in that measure. His ability to disrupt both running and passing plays gives Dennis Allen something the defense has lacked up front. But there are two parts to this trade. One is the impact Simmons can make on Sundays. The other is how Chicago builds around him in the years ahead. Two first-round picks create pressure beyond this season Aug 28, 2021; Nashville, TN, USA; Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons (98) celebrates after a defensive stop on fourth down during the first half against the Chicago Bears at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Christopher Hanewinckel-USA TODAY Sports The Bears are 5-2, Caleb Williams is playing well, and the offense has enough young talent to make a serious playoff push. General manager Ryan Poles had a strong reason to seek an established defender. A productive Simmons could force opponents to devote more attention to the middle, potentially creating better opportunities for Grady Jarrett, Montez Sweat and Chicago’s other rushers. That is the argument for paying a premium. Draft picks may eventually become stars; Simmons already is one. Poles has acquired a player who can help the Bears now and remains under contract through 2030. Still, those first-round selections were more than future lottery tickets. They were chances to add two talented players on relatively affordable rookie contracts. That matters for a team whose young offensive core will not stay inexpensive forever. Williams becomes eligible for a contract extension after this season, while other key players will eventually need new deals of their own. The Bears have also taken on Simmons’ substantial contract. ESPN’s breakdown projects his 2027 cap charge at roughly $22.55 million. Assuming his deal is not renegotiated, his 2028 charge would rise to about $30.9 million. Much of his future pay is already guaranteed or scheduled to become guaranteed, leaving Chicago with less flexibility if his performance declines. That does not make the trade a mistake. It means the Bears need Simmons to remain a high-impact player well beyond this winter. What would make the gamble worthwhile? item.title: Arsenal, Liverpool and Man United monitor Karl amid criticism at Bayern
item.description: Arsenal, Liverpool and Man United monitor Karl amid criticism at Bayern After an impressive breakthrough campaign at Bayern Munich, Lennart Karl has faced difficulties both on and off the pitch since the start of the 2026/27 season. The 18-year-old has struggled to rediscover his best form after recovering from the muscle tear that ruled him out of the World Cup. At the same time, his attitude and behaviour off the pitch have recently come under significant criticism from Bayern supervisory board member Uli Hoeneß. “I plan to have a serious word with him. He is a long way from being a superstar. Young players need humility,” Hoeneß fumed in an interview with Welt am Sonntag. “Comparisons with [Michael] Olise are clearly not doing him any good. There is still a world of difference between them.” According to Bild's head of football, Christian Falk, Karl's situation has put Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester United on alert, with all three Premier League clubs monitoring developments should an opportunity to sign the 18-year-old arise in the future. “Of course, the Premier League is also reading what is being said in Germany. I heard that Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United saw that there is something going on around Lennart Karl,” Falk said on his website, CF Bayern Insider. “Ultimately, when there’s a player at the Ballon d ‘Or ceremony who finished fourth in the Men’s Kopa Trophy (behind Warren Zaire-Emery, Pau Cubarsi and Lamine Yamal), he’s going to be interesting to other clubs. So calls have been made to ascertain what’s going on with the player and whether anyone’s not totally satisfied with the young German in Munich." However, despite the difficulties Karl has experienced this season, there is little indication that Bayern have changed their stance on the youngster or no longer see him as part of their long-term plans. When asked about the 18-year-old's dip in form on Friday, Bayern Munich assistant coach Aaron Danks reaffirmed the club's belief in him. “I've been a coach for a long time and worked a lot with young players. What Lenny's going through is completely normal. At his age, it's like a rollercoaster with ups and downs. We fully support him and push him. He's done very well in the last two games, also working back. We're calm and believe in him,” Danks said. Karl is under contract with Bayern until 2029.

item.title: Embarrassing England’s World Cup all but over after running out of steam
item.description: Mikey Lewis and Josh Feledy square up to each other in the second half when England’s chances of securing the 68-point victory they required had already vanished - Dean Lewins England 34 Papua New Guinea 12 England’s World Cup is over. Only the most pedantic mathematician would disagree after Brian McDermott’s men dismally failed to capitalise on a blistering start and give themselves a realistic chance of qualifying for the semi-finals. They beat Papua New Guinea in Sydney, but still it verged on the embarrassing. Needing a 68-point margin of victory in their final pool game to wipe out Samoa’s points-difference advantage, England burst into a 22-0 lead by racking up four tries after only 20 minutes. The Kumuls were being pummelled and at that stage it seemed that Samoa would need to beat Tonga on Sunday to stop England from advancing. But then the momentum crashed into a heap, as England spurned opportunities and even allowed plucky Papua New Guinea back into the contest. The procession went into recession. It took until the 68th minute for England to score their fifth try and by then, the underdogs had crossed for two tries of their own. GAIRO VORO! 👏#RLWC26 https://t.co/lInS5O3sWK — Rugby League World Cup 2026 (@rugbyleaguewcup) October 30, 2026 There were late scores for Morgan Knowles and Mikey Lewis, but they were scant consolation. England must hang around for the formalities, with Samoa knowing they could even lose by 46 points against their fierce Pacific Island rivals and still go through to the knockout stages. Barring a miracle this will be the first time in the 72-year history of the World Cup that England have not made the last four. So what went wrong? Well, the format was daft – no side in a World Cup should ever be forced to return after winning two of three games – and the damage was done in the first pool match when they lost to Tonga . That they offered themselves a sniff with their 82-0 defeat of France last weekend is besides the point. They had to maintain that pace to put the pressure on Samoa, but after the ideal beginning they contracted a nasty case of white-line fever from which they could not recover. item.title: AFCON’s return to a two-year cycle set to impact Premier League clubs
item.description: AFCON’s return to a two-year cycle set to impact Premier League clubs The Africa Cup of Nations will again be staged every two years after the Confederation of African Football confirmed a decision to reverse previous changes. CAF president Patrice Motsepe says the decision to bring back a two-year Africa Cup of Nations is designed to 'protect' the interests of African football, after the governing body confirmed a U-turn on its plan to stage the tournament every four years. CAF announced the reversal in a press release on Thursday night. The next editions are now scheduled for 2027, 2028, 2031 and 2033. In December 2025, Motsepe had announced that AFCON would move to a four-year cycle from 2028, with a new African Nations League due to launch in 2029. Earlier this month, he admitted talks had taken place about keeping the tournament biennial. CAF said the rethink was driven by concerns over how long the Nations League would take to become a serious source of revenue for the confederation. "The review (of the decision to make AFCON every four years instead of every two years) was motivated in particular by the observation that the proposed new pan-African competition, the Nations League, intended to replace the current AFCON and to be played every two years, would require several years before it could generate the substantial financial resources necessary to allow CAF competitions and African football to be globally competitive and financially self-sufficient." - CAF statement The decision is likely to be greeted unfavourably by European clubs. The biennial scheduling has often caused issues for Premier League and European clubs, who are obligated to release players mid-season to the tournament. Those set to be impacted by the changes include high-profile Premier Leagu e names including Bryan Mbeumo, Nicolas Jackson, Iliman Ndiaye and Mohammed Kudus. The next men's tournament will be co-hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda. The last edition remains unresolved off the pitch: Senegal beat hosts Morocco 1-0 in the final in Rabat, but CAF later ruled they had forfeited the match after their players walked off in protest at a penalty decision. The Senegalese Football Federation has taken the case to the Court of Arbitration for Sport. In his statement, Motsepe also pointed to African players based at clubs outside the continent as a consideration in the decision. "The decision by the CAF Executive Committee to reinstate the organization of the AFCON every two years aims to advance, protect and promote the interests of African football and the 54 CAF Member Associations. This is in addition to those of African players playing for clubs outside the continent. item.title: Petoskey's Lily Flynn embraced change and chance to build program for the future
item.description: PETOSKEY — Lily Flynn could have had a totally different approach to her senior season on the volleyball court. An outside hitter for Petoskey throughout her career, Flynn was asked to change positions, leaving behind the glory of racking up kills for the back row as a libero. She would also spend most of the season surrounded by players she didn’t grow up playing with, as freshmen and sophomores filled the court, including a pair that would step into that outside job. “I kept asking, ‘Yes, no? Are you good with this?’ And she was,” Petoskey coach Erin Luckhardt said. “That’s not a role that she’s played before. She’s played back row, but playing back row exclusively is different for her and she’s stepped into it and done a great job.” Flynn’s attitude to change and an up and down 2026 campaign wasn’t the kind you might expect. She embraced playing in the back, calling things out on the court and leading a young team experiencing not only varsity volleyball for the first time, but high school. “I also felt like I was more confident in myself in the back row,” Flynn said. “I think that positon fits me better.” Playoff Football Picks: High school football picks for opening round of MHSAA playoffs | Kochanny Luckhardt knew Flynn had the natural leadership abilities she needed on the defensive side, a big piece to making that move, beyond the talent she had for serve receive. “Lily, just her voice and her leadership in the back row,” Luckhardt said. “You can hear her on the court when she’s calling things. item.description: Barcelona officials ‘stunned’ by Raphinha’s Brazil national team call-up – report Raphinha’s start to the season was as explosive as starts get. The Barcelona captain simply looked unstoppable in front of goal, and momentum was on his side as he even netted back-to-back hat-tricks. Everything fell apart when he was called up for international duty by Carlo Ancelotti and used like a bar of soap against relatively unimportant opponents. The manager pushed Raphinha to the limit in the team’s games against Australia, and he eventually suffered a thigh injury that ruled him out for Barcelona’s games after the international break. Even after returning from injury, he has appeared to be a shadow of his former self and has not performed at the same level as he did before. Ancelotti shocks Barcelona again Barcelona are shocked by Raphinha’s call-up. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) As reported in an exclusive update by The Touchline , Barcelona are astonished by Carlo Ancelotti’s decision to include Raphinha in his squad for the upcoming international break in November. After all, the captain has still not completely recovered from his setback and is still not at 100% physically. To be the causative agent of his last injury and to call him up again just days after his return from injury, needless to say, is appalling. In a day and age where schedules are only getting more hectic, there simply has to be some attention given to player welfare and fitness. After all, Ancelotti has never shown any restraint in fielding the Barcelona star in Brazil’s games and has seldom even taken the player off despite finding means to rotate other big names. A long-drawn history Raphinha has a history of suffering injuries on international duty.. (Photo by Ian Hitchcock/Getty Images) What makes the situation all the more uncomfortable for Barcelona is the fact that Raphinha has a long history of picking up injuries on international duty, simply because his minutes are not managed well. Even after El Clasico , Hansi Flick confirmed that Raphinha himself asked to be taken off as his body was not able to take the load, and while the German coach unsurprisingly prioritised the winger’s fitness, the same cannot be expected from Ancelotti. This time around, Brazil are set to play in Singapore on November 14th and 17th, and the player will have to undertake a journey of close to 11,000 km just for the inconsequential friendlies. Interestingly, players from Palmeiras and Flamengo have been excluded to honour domestic commitments.

item.title: ‘Get rid of the WNBA’ – Enes Kanter lambasts Stephanie White’s trans comment
item.description: Credit: Michael Reaves/Joseph Weiser/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Enes Kanter is holding nothing back in his assessment of Stephanie White’s comments on the transgender situation. Asked about whether transgender athletes should compete in women’s sports, Stephanie White opted out of taking a firm stance, stating: “I don’t know that I would say that I’m educated enough from a scientific standpoint. I don’t ever believe that exclusion is an answer. I just don’t. I do think when we think about various levels of sport, various governing bodies of sport and things that go into that, like I said, I’m not—I’m not educated enough at the different levels. I know growing up, I played with the boys all the time.” White later pushed back against the surrounding culture-war noise consuming the team, insisting, “The hate, the fearmongering, the divisiveness that’s trying to hijack our league will not win… Love will win. Grace will win. Humility will win and kindness will win. I stand by them… Everybody else can go to hell.” However, Enes Kanter is having none of it. Enes Kanter disagrees with Stephanie White’s stance on transgenders Enes Kanter jumped straight on Stephanie White ’s admission that she wasn’t educated on the issue, using it to tear into her logic. Calling her outright clueless, Kanter claimed several pro male players are eyeing the WNBA next, arguing that if eligibility lines get blurred, they might as well scrap the WNBA entirely. Enes Kanter said: “I’ve been actually in touch with three European players, three G League players and two former NBA players. They said if they don’t change rules, we are all in. Playing dumb and pleading a lack of scientific knowledge was a smart exit ramp to avoid unnecessary smoke. item.description: England have never previously failed to reach the knockout stages of the World Cup [Getty Images] England (24) 34 Tries: Ashton, Brimson, Young, Smith, Knowles, Lewis Goals: Savala 5, Smith Papua New Guinea (0) 12 Tries: Dotoi, Voro Goals: Martin 2 England edged towards a World Cup exit after their points chase against Papua New Guinea descended into a chaotic and error-strewn 34-12 victory that will almost certainly prove insufficient in the final reckoning. Since their opening loss to Tonga, England's objective had been simple in their two remaining group games. Win and win well to have any hope of the reaching the last four. They achieved that objective against France with a crushing 82-0 triumph and looked on course to make significant inroads into the 68-point deficit they needed to make up on Samoa when they led 22-0 after 22 minutes, courtesy of tries from Matty Ashton, AJ Brimson, Dominic Young and Harry Smith. However, things went badly wrong from there on despite head coach Brian McDermott urging his players to the be patient in the build-up to this fixture. A combination of repeatedly coughing up possession and conceding penalties restored belief in the Papua New Guinea ranks and Dudley Dotoi and Gairo Voro cashed in with tries for the Kumuls as England threw away the initiative. The sight of England centre Herbie Farnworth being stripped of the ball running towards the try line moments before Mikey Lewis added another try to Morgan Knowles' second-half effort aptly summed up how things had slipped away. England were guilty of making 21 errors and delivered a performance that included just a 57% completion rate, hardly good enough at this - or any - level. It was the total opposite of the blueprint from the France game and it means England can now only reach the last four if Tonga defeat Samoa by more than 46 points. As good as Kristian Woolf's side are, that appears highly improbable given they lost 34-6 to Samoa 12 months ago in Brisbane and have not registered a win over their neighbours since 2018. item.title: Red Wings Stars Break Silence on Dylan Larkin Departure
item.description: The Detroit Red Wings are moving forward without Dylan Larkin, and two of the team’s biggest stars have made it clear that the remaining players aren’t going to let the controversy derail their season. Following Thursday night’s emotional 4-1 victory over the Chicago Blackhawks, Moritz Seider and Alex DeBrincat spoke about the challenges facing Detroit after Larkin informed the organization he would no longer play while awaiting a trade. And while neither player dismissed what Larkin has meant to the franchise, both emphasized the importance of having players who are committed to the team. Their comments offered an interesting glimpse into a locker room suddenly facing life without its former captain. Oct 24, 2026; Calgary, Alberta, CAN; Detroit Red Wings defenseman Moritz Seider (53) against the Calgary Flames during the second period at Scotiabank Saddledome. The 25-year-old defenseman also spoke about the importance of bringing in players who want to represent Detroit, while making it clear that he still hopes Larkin finds happiness elsewhere. “Whoever we get, whatever pick we get, we’ll have players that are happy to be here,” Seider said during his postgame availability . “We just have to make sure we get them ready to be part of our team.” That’s a powerful message from a player who could eventually become one of Detroit’s most important locker-room leaders. Seider wasn’t attacking Larkin personally. In fact, he acknowledged that he wants his former teammate to be happy, even if that means continuing his career somewhere else. But his message about the players remaining in Detroit was unmistakable. The Red Wings have a season to play, and they need everyone pulling in the same direction. item.description: Who is Jariyah Shah? Man United academy gem called up to training ahead of Chelsea match Michael Carrick is fighting several battles at once as Manchester United’s head coach. The season started with Carrick having one hand tied behind his back by the club’s hierarchy, who failed to address multiple problem positions. On top of that, injuries to Luke Shaw and Benjamin Sesko have exacerbated his selection headache. In recent weeks, it has emerged that there is considerable tension inside the dressing room, with Lisandro Martinez and Bruno Fernandes going public with their discontent. Fernandes was even dropped against Bournemouth for his comments questioning Carrick’s tactics. Carrick is certainly walking on thin ice, and in order to survive this disastrous run of form, his first priority should be to improve the atmosphere at Carrington. One way to do this is to inject young blood into training. Jariyah Shah called up to first-team training According to the Standard , Jariyah Shah has trained with the Manchester United senior squad ahead of their clash against Chelsea. Michael Carrick will be without Benjamin Sesko, Patrick Dorgu and Manuel Ugarte over the weekend. The likes of Marcus Rashford and Luke Shaw are also doubts for the trip to London. Injuries to a number of senior stars have opened the door for academy players to grab Carrick’s attention. It is understood that Jack Fletcher, son of former United midfielder Darren Fletcher, and Shah were spotted in training at Carrington. Who is Manchester United youngster Jariyah Shah The 17-year-old talent, who was born in Canberra, Australia, signed for United from Doncaster Rovers in 2023 along with Zac Watson and Neitan Barbosa. The Australia U17 international signed scholarship forms in 2025 and made his U18s debut for the Mancunians in February of that year. He has become a regular for United’s U18s. Shah has two goals in eight appearances to his name in the U18 Premier League this term. Naturally a midfielder, Shah has also played as a right-back at youth level. So far, only Shea Lacey has managed to pick up respectable minutes for an academy player under Carrick , but if United’s overpaid senior stars continue to disappoint, the likes of Shah may soon get an opportunity to make their first-team debut.

(Photo by Jeff Robinson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Yankees entered the offseason facing familiar questions about their offensive identity after another frustrating end to their season. Despite the talent in their lineup, the Yankees were swept by the division rival Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Division Series, leaving the franchise to confront concerns about its execution, approach and ability to deliver when the stakes are highest. item.title: Son Heung-min pushing toward postseason debut with LAFC
item.description: Son Heung-min will make his MLS postseason debut after helping the Los Angeles Football Club clinch a playoff bid. Los Angeles FC clinched a spot in the MLS playoffs after a 2-2 draw with the LA Galaxy on Sunday, Oct. 25, reaching the postseason for the eighth time in the franchise's nine-year history. “We still got two more games to play in the regular season,” Heung-min said of LAFC's fight for playoff positioning. “We want to finish as high as possible so we can have a home game as many times as possible.” LAFC have 47 points and trail the San Jose Earthquakes and the Houston Dynamo by one point in the standings, and will face Minnesota United on Nov. 1 and the Seattle Sounders on Nov. 7. Heung-min believes the black and gold missed an opportunity to tie San Jose in the standings after an offside call against teammate Denis Bouanga in the 29th minute of the first half resulted in his apparent goal being called back. “We were talking about yesterday’s games still and I feel like we deserved the three points and then especially because we created many chances,” Heung-min said. “The first goal I scored should've counted as a goal, but that was the referee’s decision. “… We also have to respect that decision. But, obviously, it is disappointing a little bit because we play at home during the playoffs.” Heung-min has seven goals and 15 assists in 29 games played this season. He is just one assist shy of setting LAFC’s single-season assists record set by Carlos Vela in 2019 when he was named the MLS MVP. Heung-min sets South Korea scoring record Heung-min captained South Korea in the World Cup earlier this year as the country finished 1-0-3 and was eliminated in the group stage. After the elimination, Heung-min expressed how "indescribably hurt" he was. He did manage to break South Korea’s all-time scoring record, producing his 59th international goal during a friendly match against Uzbekistan. "It was a huge honor. ... I was never thinking about it when I started in the national team," he said. "After 16 years in the national team, I'm the top scorer.” Heung-min integrating with LA community off the pitch Heung-min has spent parts of two seasons in Los Angeles and continues to ingratiate himself with the community. In the hours that followed the El Tráfico draw, the 34-year-old partnered with Chime and Knowlej to visit with Fairfax High School in Los Angeles. The event was intended to help provide school attendance incentives and financial education programming to local area schools. Heung-min’s mission was to meet with approximately 200 students during a school assembly and help them stay motivated and invested in their future while sharing his own journey and adversity. “It just feels weird coming back to the school, but it makes me really excited to see all the students,” Heung-min said. item.title: Fernando Alonso launches scathing attack on ‘low-level’ F1 drivers
item.description: Fernando Alonso has doubled down on his criticism of “low-level” drivers on the Formula 1 grid, insisting they simply have a “lack of talent.” The two-time world champion, who has been languishing at the back of the field this year with Aston Martin, was embroiled in an on-track battle with Williams ’ Alex Albon last Sunday at the US Grand Prix. Albon went into the side of Alonso’s car on lap one, damaging both cars, prompting Alonso to claim post-race that the standard of drivers in the bottom third of the grid was “very low.” Yet when asked about his outburst on Thursday ahead of this weekend’s grand prix in Mexico City , the 45-year-old refused to renege on his opinions. "I think it's simply a very low level of driving and lack of talent," he said. "When you make repeated mistakes throughout the season and have crashes and 50 per cent of your race is in lap one... if I was the team principal I would not be happy. But if they are happy, I'm OK with that. "When I see Max [Verstappen], Lewis [Hamilton] starting at the back when they change the engine or whatever, Kimi in Monza, they still win the races. Lap one is not the end of the world when you have your confidence and the talent to wait for one or two more laps." When asked about the comments, 30-year-old Albon – who raced for Red Bull prior to Williams – admitted it “wasn’t nice to hear” but simply opined that he didn’t agree with the outspoken Spaniard. "I'll double down with what I said as well,” Albon said in the FIA press conference. “I have a huge respect for Fernando. I looked up to him a lot growing up as a kid," said the Williams driver. Alonso clashed with Alex Albon (left) in Austin (Getty) "It's not nice to hear those comments in many ways. You're racing someone that you look up to, but at the same time, I don't agree. It's as simple as that. "I think level is strong up and down the grid. I think 10, 15 years ago, the back half the grid wasn't the way it is now. We don't have pay drivers anymore. It is what it is. Hopefully, we don't cross corners or cross paths in the race this weekend!" Alonso, who has just seven points to his name this season, is teammates with Lance Stroll, the son of Aston Martin executive chairman Lawrence Stroll. Stroll is one of three drivers, alongside the Cadillac pair of Sergio Perez and Valtteri Bottas, who is yet to score a point this year.

A centerpiece name of these reports? Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Patrick Queen. This movement seems to have been triggered by ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler having named the Cowboys as the “Top Trade Fit” for a player in Queen who during his career has been an NFL All-Pro and a two-time Pro Bowler. Along with his report, though, Fowler carefully walked the tightrope of truth by both predicting a "20-percent chance'' of a trade and writing, "The Steelers’ status as a 5-2 team likely keeps him in Pittsburgh.” Clever. item.description: Cameron Boozer's first NBA triple-double sends powerful message about Grizzlies' future originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Memphis Grizzlies made one of the NBA's biggest decisions during the offseason when they traded Ja Morant to the Portland Trail Blazers . Morant had been the face of the franchise for years, and his departure created immediate questions about the organization's future. Who would become the centerpiece of the next era? How quickly could Memphis develop a competitive identity without its former star? And would its young players be ready to handle additional responsibility? Thursday night provided another encouraging answer. Rookie Cameron Boozer recorded the first triple-double of his NBA career, finishing with 18 points, 12 rebounds and 12 assists as the Grizzlies defeated Portland 124-103. The victory improved Memphis to 5-0 and ended the Trail Blazers' undefeated start. It also provided a striking contrast between the franchise's past and future. Boozer dominates without needing huge scoring night Boozer's 18 points were only part of his contribution. The rookie controlled the game through his passing, rebounding and ability to create opportunities for teammates. CAM BOOZER TRIPLE-DOUBLE. GRIZZLIES STAY UNDEFEATED. Rather than forcing difficult shots, Boozer repeatedly helped Memphis find productive offensive possessions. That approach fits the identity the Grizzlies are beginning to establish. Memphis received double-figure scoring contributions from eight players, demonstrating that the team does not need one superstar to carry the entire offensive burden. Isaiah Stewart contributed 18 points off the bench, while Cedric Coward added 17. The Grizzlies also received contributions from established players including Zach Edey and Ty Jerome. item.description: Bayern were ready to splash €72m on Liverpool star before turning to Saibari Bayern Munich were linked with a move for Liverpool wonderkid Rio Ngumoha last summer, but the transfer ultimately failed to materialise. item.description: Christian Watson played a pivotal role in the Green Bay Packers ‘ 27-19 home win over the Carolina Panthers in Week 8. Beyond another productive outing, Watson also gave the Cheeseheads something to write home about during the “Thursday Night Football” matchup. What happened to Green Bay Packers WR Christian Watson vs. Carolina Panthers? Oct 29, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson (9) is tackled by Carolina Panthers cornerback Will Lee III (24) and safety Zakee Wheatley (20) on a pass reception during their football game at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Wm. Glasheen USA Today Network via IMAGN Images Christian Watson suffered a broken rib after making a deep catch early in the second quarter for 53 yards. Watson fought for position with Carolina Panthers cornerback Will Lee III, who suffered a hamstring injury after landing hard on Watson’s chest. Watson, who coughed up blood, eventually walked off the field and hopped into an ambulance to get checked at a hospital. “I think I just came down on the ball or my elbow or something,” Watson told ESPN’s Rob Demovsky. “I couldn’t breathe on the field. I got the wind knocked out of me. I got back to the sideline, and I was kind of spitting up some blood or something like that. So the doctor said I had to go get a CT. He took a hard fall when he didn’t catch it, and fans at Lambeau Field held their breath, but Watson popped back up and added 13 more receiving yards to his total. “It was super dramatic. I used to watch WWE as a kid. I felt like I was watching WWE Smackdown vs. Raw or something, seeing the cameras on me when I was coming out of the ambulance. That was a little crazy. item.description: Lazio to Change Designated Penalty Kick Taker After Sassuolo Fiasco Lazio may have scored six goals at the Mapei Stadium, but Mattia Zaccagni and Davide Frattesi’s poor penalty kicks blemished an otherwise superb outing. Lazio Wasted Two Penalties Against Sassuolo The Lazio captain was one of the main stars of the show in Tuesday’s 6-2 victory over Sassuolo, scoring a goal and providing an assist. But early in the second half, he failed to beat Stefano Turati from the spot. The 31-year-old aimed at the left corner, but couldn’t put enough power behind it, allowing the goalkeeper to gather. Watch: Lazio Pummel Sassuolo in Eight-Goal Thriller – The Highlights A few minutes later, Gustav Isaksen was brought down inside the box. While this could have been an opportunity for Zaccagni to atone, he decided to leave it to Frattesi, whose effort was even worse than the skipper’s. The midfielder sent a tame shot down the middle, allowing Turati to make the easiest of penalty saves. Mattia Zaccagni Relieved From Spot-Kick Duty? According to La Repubblica (via La Lazio Siamo Noi ), Gennaro Gattuso is expected to change his spot-kick hierarchy. While Zaccagni has been the designated kicker since Ciro Immobile’s departure in 2024, the captain could be dropped after squandering two of his last three. As for Frattesi, this was his first-ever penalty kick at the senior level, and his poor attempt is unlikely to earn him another chance in the near future. Kenneth Taylor to Become Designated Lazio Penalty Taker? The newspaper tips Kenneth Taylor to be propelled to the top of the list. The Dutchman wasn’t on the pitch when the two penalties were awarded, as Gattuso had hooked him at half-time after earning a yellow card. Nevertheless, the Italian head coach made sure to laud the midfielder for his elusive qualities after the game. Taylor’s Penalty Stats Based on Transfermarkt’s stats , the former Ajax man successfully converted 14 out of 16 career spot-kicks during the game. Last season, he scored the decisive kick in the penalty shootout against Bologna in the Coppa Italia quarter-finals . He also successfully converted his attempt in the shootout against Atalanta, which secured Lazio’s spot in the cup final.

item.title: Detroit Red Wings Laying Foundations for New Identity
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Red Wings , despite the limited expectations set in front of them before the 2026-27 began, have found themselves at the end of the first month of the season one win away from a .500 record. That’s despite the fact that the team is missing a captain on ice, and now has two disgruntled players sitting out of the lineup as they await a trade. Still, their surprisingly strong start seems to be the results of an identity and culture taking root amongst the roster that in years past, simply did not present itself. “We’re developing an identity. I can’t say that my first year in a bit that we really had an identity.” Head coach Todd McLellan said after the team’s 4-1 victory over Patrick Kane and the Chicago Blackhawks. “We tried to get to it, but we never did. I think we’re starting to develop one, and if the groundwork is being laid, that means we’re having a good start. Forget about points and playoffs and everything else.” Not point-less It’s still early in the season for Detroit , and this is a squad that has seemingly improved out of the gate only to suffer a disappointing March collapse that for the past three years has kept the Red Wings out of the playoffs. However, the Red Wings are playing the right kind of hockey, keeping the scores close, and taking the opportunities they’re presented, even if they’re not the cleanest looks. “We might not be the most skilled team, but we’re sticking together. We’re playing as a 5-man unit out there, and it’s showing,” Alex DeBrincat said, “We’re scoring goals, some dirty goals, and finding a way to get some points.” The Red Wings certainly aren’t headlining as playoff contenders this year, but they’re winning close games, and have so far only let in seven third period goals across the first thirteen games of their season. item.description: Ja Morant's first game against Grizzlies takes painful turn after Trail Blazers star exits originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Ja Morant's first game against the Memphis Grizzlies was always going to attract attention. The former face of the franchise spent seven seasons in Memphis, developed into one of the NBA's most electrifying guards and became one of basketball's most recognizable personalities. His departure in June marked a significant change for both Morant and the organization that selected him with the second overall pick in the 2019 NBA Draft. Thursday night provided the first opportunity for the two sides to face each other. Unfortunately for Morant, the reunion did not end the way he hoped. The Portland Trail Blazers guard exited with a left hamstring injury during the fourth quarter of a 124-103 loss to Memphis. The result ended Portland's unbeaten start while the Grizzlies improved to 5-0. For Morant, the concern surrounding his health became more important than the outcome. INJURY UPDATE: Ja Morant (L Hamstring) will not return to tonight’s game vs. MEM. — Trail Blazers PR (@TrailBlazersPR) October 30, 2026 He exited with 7:46 remaining in the fourth quarter and did not return. Portland coach Micah Nori said afterward that Morant had felt discomfort in his hamstring and was being evaluated. Nori expressed hope that the injury would not be serious but did not provide a definitive diagnosis or recovery timetable. That distinction matters. A hamstring injury can vary considerably in severity, and Morant's availability for upcoming games cannot be determined without additional medical information. Portland will have to wait for further evaluation before understanding how much time, if any, its star guard might miss. Memphis reunion carried unusual significance Morant's history with the Grizzlies makes Thursday's injury particularly unfortunate. He won NBA Rookie of the Year honors in 2019-20 and later earned the league's Most Improved Player award. During the 2021-22 season, he averaged a career-high 27.4 points per game while helping Memphis establish itself as a dangerous Western Conference team. His career also included injuries and suspensions that complicated his relationship with the organization. On June 29, Memphis traded Morant to Portland in a deal that sent Jerami Grant and Kris Murray to the Grizzlies. The move represented a new beginning for Morant and a significant roster reset for Memphis. Thursday's game provided an early look at how the two teams have changed.
